items.title: Towards Efficient HPC Systems for Agents: Challenges and Opportunities
items.summary: Coding agents have become real users of high-performance computing (HPC) systems, yet today's HPC abstractions, interfaces, and policies remain designed for human-driven workflows. In our measurement, users running coding agents are only 19.5% of the observed population, but account for 55.8% of job submissions, 29.1% of CPU core-hours, and 42.7% of GPU-hours. Agents are not simply faster humans.
